title: WPMS/1548/2013 of Bahadur Singh Patani Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1548 of 2013 (M/S)
Bahadur Singh Patni Ö..Petitioner.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others
 ......Ö.Respondents.
Present:
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Subhash Upadhyay, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Sharad Sharma, Senior Advocate assisted by Ms. Vandana Singh,
Advocate for respondent no. 4.
Honíble Alok Singh, J (Oral).
Petitioner submitted tender documents/bid pursuant
to e-tender notice dated 1.5.2013 for work of improvement and
reconstruction of Jamour - Bandiya - Khudaganj Motor Road
under State Sector at Khatima, District Udham Singh Nagar.
Undisputedly, as per one of the conditions of tender
notice, all the bidders were required to furnish FDRs or bank
drafts of `3,00,000/- in favour of Executive Engineer,
Construction Division, Public Works Department, Khatima,
District Udham Singh Nagar. Petitioner deposited four FDRs,
photo copies thereof are available at page No. 26 and 27 of the
paper book, as well as one bank draft of `1,705/-, photo copy of
which is available on the paper book as page no. 28.
Mr. Subhash Upadhyay, learned Standing Counsel
appearing for the State submits that first of all FDRs are not in the
name of Executive Engineer, Construction Division, Public Works
Department, Khatima. Secondly, perusal of page no. 26 of the
paper book would reveal that there are over-writings on the FDRs
and overwriting does not contain any initial or seal of the
competent officer of the bank, therefore, petitionerís bid was not
considered and bid of respondent no. 4 was accepted.
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned counsel appearing for the
petitioner submits that for the fault of the bank officers by not

2
putting initials and seal on the overwriting made on the FDRs,
photo copies thereof is Annexure No. 3 , page no. 26 of the paper
book, petitioner should not be made to suffer adversely and
respondent nos. 1 to 3 ought to have granted time to petitioner to
rectify the mistake or to file a certificate.
Since, there is no condition in e-tender notice for
giving opportunity for rectification or for removing the defects in
the tender documents furnished by the bidders, therefore, no fault
can be attributed on the part of respondent nos. 1 to 3.
Petitionerís bid was of `1,41,66,204/- while bid of
respondent no. 4 was of `1,48,76,809/-. There seems to be a
difference of `7,10,605/- i.e. approximately 5 %.
Difference of `7,00,000/- shall go to demonstrate that
for the meager amount of `7,00,000/- respondent nos. 1 to 3
would not have acted malafidely, therefore, rejection of bid of the
petitioner on the ground that FDRs contain overwriting, without
there being any initial and seal of the bank officials seems to be
justified. Therefore, keeping in view the meager amount of
`7,00,000/- and keeping in view that Government work should
not suffer, I do not want to interfere in the decision taken by the
respondent nos. 1 to 3 by rejecting the bid of the petitioner and by
awarding the contract in favour of respondent no. 4.
Consequently, writ petition fails and is hereby
dismissed.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
 25.2.2014
Avneet
